words.group: Word roots: tele-, trans-, super-, inter-, bio-, geo-
words.childMeaning: A machine that lets you speak to somebody far away.
practiceSentences: The telephone rang just as we sat down to eat.
Who answered the telephone this morning?
Amal used the telephone to call her grandmother.
A telephone line runs along the edge of the road.
Before the telephone, people sent letters instead.

words.group: Word roots: tele-, trans-, super-, inter-, bio-, geo-
words.childMeaning: Ways of carrying people or goods from one place to another.
practiceSentences: Buses are the cheapest transport in our town.
Which transport do you use to reach school?
Public transport was busy on Friday morning.
The city needs better transport for everyone.
Lorries transport food to the market each day.

words.group: Word roots: tele-, trans-, super-, inter-, bio-, geo-
words.childMeaning: A large shop that sells food and many other everyday things.
practiceSentences: Mum bought rice and oil at the supermarket.
Is the supermarket open on Sunday?
The new supermarket has twelve checkouts.
Amal pushed the trolley round the supermarket.
A supermarket sells far more than a small shop.

words.group: Word roots: tele-, trans-, super-, inter-, bio-, geo-
words.childMeaning: Involving more than one country.
practiceSentences: Football is an international game.
Have you ever taken an international flight?
The school held an international food day.
An international team studied the coral reef.
English is used for international business.

words.group: Word roots: tele-, trans-, super-, inter-, bio-, geo-
words.childMeaning: The true story of a real person's life, written by somebody else.
practiceSentences: Nora read a biography of a famous doctor.
Whose biography did you choose for your project?
The biography described his childhood in detail.
A biography is written about someone, not by them.
Maya is writing a short biography of her grandmother.

words.group: Word roots: tele-, trans-, super-, inter-, bio-, geo-
words.childMeaning: The study of the Earth, its countries, and the people who live there.
practiceSentences: Geography is my favourite subject at school.
What did you learn in geography today?
The geography of the island makes farming hard.
Our geography lesson covered rivers and mountains.
Maps are an important tool in geography.

words.group: Words: devices, data and being online
words.childMeaning: A small part that you press to make a machine or device work.
practiceSentences: Press the green button to start the machine.
Which button turns the volume down?
Amal pressed the button and the lift moved.
A red button stops the whole conveyor belt.
Do not press that button without asking first.

words.group: Words: devices, data and being online
words.childMeaning: A word or picture you tap to open another page online.
practiceSentences: Tap the blue link to open the article.
Where does this link take you?
Nora sent me a link to the weather page.
A broken link leads to nothing at all.
The link at the bottom opens the whole report.

words.group: Words: devices, data and being online
words.childMeaning: Connected to the internet.
practiceSentences: Amal is online, so we can send a message.
Are the results online yet?
The shop sells its books online as well.
Stay safe when you are online.
Our lesson moved online during the storm.

words.group: Words: devices, data and being online
words.childMeaning: A secret word or set of letters that lets only you sign in.
practiceSentences: Never tell anyone your password.
Have you forgotten your password again?
A strong password mixes letters and numbers.
Nora changed her password every month.
The password must be at least eight letters.

words.group: Words: devices, data and being online
words.childMeaning: A machine that can be programmed to do a job by itself.
practiceSentences: The robot picked up the block and moved it.
Can a robot really tidy a whole room?
Nora built a robot from a kit at the club.
A robot follows the code you write for it.
This robot vacuums the floor every morning.

words.group: Words: devices, data and being online
words.childMeaning: A recording of moving pictures and sound.
practiceSentences: We watched a video about the water cycle.
Did you record a video of the concert?
The video lasted only three minutes.
Amal made a short video for her project.
A video can explain a machine better than words.

words.group: Words that place something in time
words.childMeaning: A short time ago.
practiceSentences: Amal recently joined the reading club.
Have you recently changed your password?
The school recently bought twenty tablets.
Leo recently learned to write simple code.
We recently moved to a house near the market.

words.group: Words that place something in time
words.childMeaning: At this moment; right now.
practiceSentences: The website is currently closed for repairs.
What are you currently reading, Nora?
Sami is currently working on his project.
The network is currently very slow.
We are currently learning about the water cycle.

words.group: Words that place something in time
words.childMeaning: Right away, without waiting at all.
practiceSentences: Idris wanted to use the telescope immediately.
Can you come here immediately?
Amal, put that down immediately!
The class immediately began cleaning the attic.
Reply immediately if the message is urgent.

words.childMeaning: Telling the truth and not hiding anything.
practiceSentences: Is it always easy to be honest?
Omar gave an honest answer to every question.
Be honest, Sami, even when it is hard!
Her honest report impressed the whole class.
An honest player admits when the ball is out.

words.childMeaning: Treating people kindly because you value who they are.
practiceSentences: Amal learned to show respect to every worker in town.
Why is respect so important in a community?
What great respect the children showed the caretaker!
The teacher spoke about respect before the parade.
We show respect by listening while others speak.

words.childMeaning: A strong belief that someone is honest and will not let you down.
practiceSentences: Amal earned her teacher's trust through hard work.
Do you trust your best friend with a secret?
What great trust the whole class showed her!
Sami said trust takes time to build.
It takes time to earn trust, and one lie to lose it.

words.childMeaning: To forgive means to stop being cross with someone.
practiceSentences: Amal chose to forgive Leo for breaking her pencil.
It is kind to forgive a friend who says sorry.
“Please forgive me,” said Nora quietly.
Grandma said we should forgive and stay friends.
Leo asked his sister to forgive him.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Feeling a little cross about something that keeps bothering you.
practiceSentences: Sami felt annoyed when his pencil broke again.
Why do you look so annoyed this morning?
The buzzing fly annoyed everyone in the room.
Mum was annoyed that the taps were left running.
I get annoyed when my brother hides my shoes.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Happy and bright in the way you look, speak and act.
practiceSentences: Nora gave us a cheerful wave from the gate.
What a cheerful song that is!
The cheerful yellow walls made the room feel warm.
Teacher Yasmin has a cheerful voice in the morning.
Even in the rain, Leo stayed cheerful all day.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Delighted means feeling very happy and pleased about something.
practiceSentences: Nora looked delighted with her finished project.
Were you delighted with your test result?
Teacher Yasmin smiled, absolutely delighted with the class!
The whole team felt delighted after the win.
Grandma Hana was delighted with the card we made.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Frightened means feeling scared or afraid of something.
practiceSentences: The little dog looked frightened during the storm.
Were you frightened when the lights went out?
Nora hugged her sister, who seemed frightened!
A calm voice can help a frightened child feel safe.
The frightened kitten hid under the stairs.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Feeling thankful for something kind that someone has done.
practiceSentences: We are grateful for our teachers.
Are you grateful for your friends?
How grateful he looked after the help!
Sami felt grateful for the cold juice.
Omar looked surprised and grateful.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Feeling upset because someone else has something you want.
practiceSentences: Sami felt jealous of his sister's new bicycle.
Are you jealous that Nora won the prize?
A jealous feeling is hard, but it soon passes.
Leo tried not to feel jealous of the winning team.
Amal was jealous until she remembered her own gift.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Feeling very sad and unhappy for a while.
practiceSentences: Losing his football boot made Leo miserable.
Why did Amal look so miserable this morning?
Cold rain and a long walk made a miserable day.
Nobody likes to feel miserable for very long.
A warm drink helped the miserable puppy settle.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Calm, quiet and free from fighting or trouble.
practiceSentences: The garden behind the school is very peaceful.
Is the town square peaceful in the early morning?
What a peaceful evening this is!
A peaceful street makes children feel safe.
The lake looked peaceful in the early light.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: If you feel pleased, you feel happy and glad about something that happened.
practiceSentences: Sami felt pleased after sharing his idea.
Was Teacher Yasmin pleased with the class?
Amal's mother was very pleased with her.
What a pleased smile that is!
Nora looked pleased with her finished painting.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Calm and comfortable, with nothing making you worried.
practiceSentences: Amal felt relaxed after the long swim.
Do you feel relaxed on a Friday afternoon?
The relaxed cat slept in the warm sunshine.
Leo looked relaxed once the test was over.
Slow breathing helps me feel relaxed again.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Quiet and a little afraid to talk to people you do not know.
practiceSentences: The shy new girl stood alone beside the wall.
The shy new student ate lunch alone at first.
Were you shy on your first day of school?
"Do not be shy; come join our game," said Theo.
I was too shy to sing, so I hummed quietly instead.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Happy to share what you have, or to give things to others.
practiceSentences: It was generous of Nora to lend me her coat.
The generous baker gave extra bread to the poor family.
Who was generous enough to share their umbrella today?
"A generous heart is never empty," said the teacher.
My generous friend gave me half of her sandwich.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Only caring about yourself and not about how other people feel.
practiceSentences: Keeping the whole box of crayons would be selfish.
The selfish king in the story kept all the water.
Is it selfish to want the swing all break time?
"Sharing stops us from being selfish," said Mother.
I felt selfish after hiding the coloured pencils, so I apologised.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Showing good sense and thinking carefully before you act.
practiceSentences: Leo made a sensible suggestion about the vote.
Was that a sensible choice, Amal?
What a sensible idea, Sami!
It is sensible to wear a coat in the rain.
A sensible plan saves time later.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Kind, because you stop and think about what other people need.
practiceSentences: It was thoughtful of Amal to help Sami try again.
The thoughtful boy saved a seat for his friend.
Was it thoughtful of Maya to share her umbrella?
Mum said, "A thoughtful guest brings a small gift."
I was thoughtful and carried Grandma's shopping home.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Not nice or gentle, and likely to hurt someone's feelings.
practiceSentences: Leo's brother never says an unkind word.
Was that comment unkind or just honest?
How unkind that joke was!
Nobody wants to be unkind to a new pupil.
An unkind word can hurt for a long time.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Not fair or right; treating someone in a way that they do not deserve.
practiceSentences: Amal made sure her report was never unfair.
Was the decision unfair to the other team?
What an unfair way to end the match!
Sami thought the new rule seemed unfair.
It is unfair when only one side gets a turn.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: The warm feeling between people who are friends.
practiceSentences: Their friendship began on the very first day.
What makes a friendship last a long time?
A true friendship survives a small argument.
Amal values her friendship with Nora most of all.
Sharing and listening help a friendship grow.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: The way a person acts towards other people.
practiceSentences: Kind behaviour helps everyone feel safe at school.
Good behaviour means sharing, listening, and speaking kindly.
Was your behaviour kind during playtime today?
The teacher said, "Your behaviour made me very proud."
My behaviour improves when I remember to be patient.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: A moment when people do not think the same thing.
practiceSentences: A small disagreement began over the last chair.
How did you settle the disagreement, Sami?
Their disagreement ended with a friendly handshake.
The class had a disagreement about the new rule.
A disagreement is not the same as a quarrel.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: The act of being kind and helpful to somebody.
practiceSentences: One small act of kindness can start many more.
What kindness did you notice in the playground today?
“Kindness is free, so give extra when you can,” said Nora.
My jar of kindness notes is almost full now.
Teacher Yasmin thanked the class for their kindness to Amal.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: People working together to finish a job or reach a goal.
practiceSentences: Tools help us, but teamwork builds the best things of all.
Why is teamwork so important in science club?
Amal, that was excellent teamwork today!
The whole class showed great teamwork on the model.
Good teamwork made the heavy job feel light.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: A person you have never met before.
practiceSentences: Never walk away with a stranger, said Mum.
Was the visitor a stranger or a friend?
A kind stranger helped Amal find the station.
The stranger at the gate turned out to be Uncle.
Sami felt shy talking to a stranger.

words.childMeaning: In a fast way, taking little time.
practiceSentences: The rain clouds moved quickly across the sky.
How quickly can you finish the diagram?
Amal quickly wrote down the temperature.
Water evaporates quickly on a hot day.
The storm passed more quickly than we expected.

words.childMeaning: Taking a long time; at a gentle pace.
practiceSentences: The glacier moves slowly down the valley.
Why does the puddle dry so slowly today?
Leo slowly poured the water into the jar.
Heavy clouds drifted slowly over the hill.
Read the instructions slowly and carefully.

words.childMeaning: Without making much noise.
practiceSentences: Snow fell quietly through the whole night.
Can you close the door quietly, please?
Nora quietly watched the bird build its nest.
The stream ran quietly under the bridge.
Sami quietly recorded the wind speed each hour.

words.childMeaning: In a way that makes a lot of noise.
practiceSentences: Thunder rumbled loudly above the school.
Why is the wind howling so loudly tonight?
The rain drummed loudly on the metal roof.
Amal read her weather report loudly and clearly.
Waves crashed loudly against the rocks.

words.childMeaning: Happening quickly, without any warning.
practiceSentences: The sky suddenly darkened before the storm.
Did the wind suddenly change direction?
Rain suddenly began during the football match.
The temperature dropped suddenly after sunset.
Leo suddenly noticed frost on the window.

words.childMeaning: Close to where you are, not far away.
practiceSentences: A nearby stream feeds the village well.
Is there a nearby shelter from the rain?
The nearby hills were covered in mist.
Birds nest in the nearby trees each spring.
We measured rainfall at a nearby station.

words.childMeaning: Completely different from something, or on the other side of it.
practiceSentences: Evaporation is the opposite of condensation.
Which word is the opposite of visible?
The wind blew from the opposite direction.
Their results were the opposite of ours.
The shop stands opposite the weather station.

words.childMeaning: Directly below or under something.
practiceSentences: Worms live underneath the top layer of soil.
What is hiding underneath that rock?
The cat sheltered underneath the bench.
Cool air settles underneath the warm air.
Nora found frost underneath the fallen leaves.

words.childMeaning: A community is all the people who live in one place.
practiceSentences: Our community keeps the park clean.
Everyone in the community came to the fair.
Amal is proud of her community.
The community built a new playground.
A community works best when people help.

words.childMeaning: A book that lists words and explains what they mean.
practiceSentences: Does Omar own a dictionary at home?
Amal won a dictionary for her writing.
What a thick dictionary that is, Sami!
Nora looked up the word in her dictionary.
A dictionary would help her learn faster.

words.childMeaning: A book you use in class to learn about a subject.
practiceSentences: Our science textbook explains how volcanoes work.
Which page of the textbook shows the diagram?
Sami covered his new textbook with brown paper.
Leave your textbook open at chapter nine.
The maths textbook has answers at the back.

words.childMeaning: A numbered part of a book that tells one section of the story.
practiceSentences: Amal read a whole chapter under the mango tree.
Which chapter are you reading tonight?
Wow, Leo finished that long chapter in a single day!
The last chapter explained how the library cart began.
Each chapter of the book ends with a question.

words.childMeaning: The list at the front of a book that shows what is inside.
practiceSentences: Check the contents page to find the chapter.
Where is the contents list in this book?
The contents show every chapter in order.
Amal used the contents to find the poem quickly.
A good contents page saves you a lot of time.

words.childMeaning: The title written at the top of a page or a piece of writing.
practiceSentences: Write a clear heading at the top of your page.
What heading did you choose for your report?
Each heading is written in bigger letters.
Amal underlined the heading with a red pen.
A good heading tells you what the part is about.

words.childMeaning: A label is a short piece of writing that names or explains a picture or object.
practiceSentences: Every picture needs one clear label.
Where is the label for this chart, Sami?
What a tidy label, Leo!
I added a label to each page of my folder.
Add one picture and one clear label to each page.

words.childMeaning: A simple drawing that explains how something works.
practiceSentences: The diagram showed each part of the plant.
Can you label every part of this diagram?
Sami copied the diagram into his notebook.
A clear diagram is easier than a long explanation.
Our textbook has a diagram of the human ear.

words.childMeaning: A chart is a drawing or diagram that shows information clearly.
practiceSentences: Nora told everyone to look at their moisture chart.
Did you finish the rainfall chart yet?
Amal added new numbers to the chart.
What a clear chart this is!
The chart shows how much rain fell each month.

words.childMeaning: A drawing that uses bars or lines to compare numbers.
practiceSentences: The graph shows how much rain fell each month.
Which month is highest on the graph?
Nora drew a graph of our favourite fruits.
A graph makes the numbers easy to compare.
Read the graph carefully before you answer.

words.childMeaning: A photograph is a picture taken with a camera.
practiceSentences: Amal has seen a photograph of snow on a mountain.
Do you have a photograph of the trip?
What a lovely photograph this is!
Sami printed the photograph for his project.
Amal framed the photograph of her grandmother.

words.childMeaning: A place on the internet where you can read or watch things.
practiceSentences: Our school website shows the term dates.
Which website did you use for your project?
The website has a photograph of every class.
Nora built a website about her favourite birds.
A safe website is one your teacher has checked.

words.childMeaning: A collection of information kept together, often written down or on paper.
practiceSentences: Leo added a new page to the science file.
Is your animal file finished yet, Amal?
What a neat file you have made!
Nora kept a file of every plant she found.
Keep your best work safe in a project file.

words.childMeaning: A cover or container used to hold papers and keep them tidy.
practiceSentences: Amal slid her drawings into a card folder before the bell rang.
Each project sits in its own coloured folder on the shelf.
Did you put the permission slip in your folder?
“Bring your reading folder every Monday,” said Teacher Yasmin.
My folder ripped, so Father helped me tape it.

words.childMeaning: A piece of writing that holds important information.
practiceSentences: Dad signed the document at the office.
Is this document the one we need today?
The document listed every child in the class.
Amal typed a short document about her hobby.
Keep the document safe inside the folder.

words.childMeaning: A machine that puts writing or pictures onto paper.
practiceSentences: The printer made a loud noise and stopped.
Is there any paper left in the printer?
Sami sent his story to the printer.
Our printer can print in black or colour.
Wait by the printer for your photograph.

words.childMeaning: A flat screen you touch to read, watch and play.
practiceSentences: The words on the tablet are big and clear.
May I read my story on the tablet?
“Put the tablet down at bedtime,” said Amal's mother.
I play a spelling game on my tablet with my father.
Our class shares one tablet for the word hunt.

words.childMeaning: A machine is something built with parts that work together to do a job.
practiceSentences: Sami built a small machine out of cardboard.
How does this machine actually work?
Wow, Maya, that machine can fly!
A strange machine stood in the corner of the workshop.
The washing machine hummed all afternoon.

words.childMeaning: A tool is a thing you use with your hands to help you do a job.
practiceSentences: Sami picked up the right tool for the job.
Which tool do we need to open this box?
Look at that huge tool, Nora!
Every tool in the shed has its own special place.
A hammer is the best tool for driving nails.

words.childMeaning: Things that are used for a special job or task, like tools or machines.
practiceSentences: Our sports equipment lives in the big cupboard beside the school hall.
The builders locked their equipment in the van overnight.
Where is the camping equipment kept during winter?
"Check the safety equipment before we sail," said the captain.
I cleaned the gardening equipment after we planted the seedlings.

words.childMeaning: A piece of work you plan and finish over some time.
practiceSentences: Our class project is about African animals.
When is your project due, Nora?
Amal spent two weeks on her science project.
A good project needs a plan before you start.
Sami showed his project to the whole school.

words.childMeaning: Something you do, for fun or for learning.
practiceSentences: My favourite activity is painting.
Which activity will you choose today?
The first activity was a spelling game.
Every activity in the book has a picture.
Swimming is a healthy activity for children.

words.childMeaning: A job you are asked to finish.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin gave the class a writing task.
Have you finished your task yet, Leo?
The task took only ten minutes to complete.
Each task is written on the board.
Amal likes a task she can do on her own.

words.childMeaning: One thing that shows what the others are like.
practiceSentences: Give me one example of a wild animal.
Can you think of an example, Sami?
The teacher wrote an example on the board.
This poem is a good example of a rhyme.
Amal used an example to explain her idea.

words.childMeaning: A statement that tells you what to do.
practiceSentences: Amal followed every instruction carefully at the market.
What was the teacher's instruction for the homework?
The recipe had a simple instruction about washing the rice.
Noah forgot the last instruction his grandmother gave him.
Read each instruction twice before you begin.

words.childMeaning: What happens in the end, because of what came before.
practiceSentences: The result of the match was a draw.
What was the result of your experiment?
Amal waited nervously for the result.
Hard work gave Sami a better result.
We wrote the result at the bottom of the chart.

words.childMeaning: Something you get wrong by accident.
practiceSentences: Everybody makes a mistake now and then.
Was that a mistake or a good guess?
Leo spotted one spelling mistake on the poster.
A mistake helps you learn if you fix it.
Amal made no mistake in her whole test.

words.childMeaning: A change you make to put a mistake right.
practiceSentences: Write your correction neatly underneath.
Did you make the correction in red pen?
One small correction fixed the whole sentence.
Teacher Yasmin marked a correction on my page.
A correction shows that you have learned.

words.childMeaning: In a glad and cheerful way.
practiceSentences: The children happily shared the fresh fruit.
Did Leo happily agree to help with lunch?
Amal happily finished her bowl of soup.
Nora happily wrote down the whole recipe.
They happily walked home after the meal.

words.childMeaning: In a way that shows you feel unhappy.
practiceSentences: Sami sadly put the spoiled fruit in the bin.
Why did she look at the empty plate so sadly?
Leo sadly admitted he had skipped breakfast.
The puppy sadly watched us eat our lunch.
Nora sadly said the bread had gone stale.

words.childMeaning: In a way that avoids harm or danger.
practiceSentences: Store the milk safely in the cold fridge.
How can we safely carry the hot pot?
Amal safely washed the fruit before eating.
Cooked meat must be stored safely overnight.
Leo safely crossed the road to the market.

words.childMeaning: Believing that something good will happen.
practiceSentences: Nora felt hopeful about her health test result.
Are you hopeful that the crop will grow well?
A hopeful smile spread across Sami's face.
The doctor was hopeful about his recovery.
Amal stayed hopeful even after a poor harvest.

words.childMeaning: Feeling that nothing will get better, however hard you keep trying.
practiceSentences: One child felt hopeless while his father was ill.
The team felt hopeless until the very last goal.
Do you feel hopeless when a puzzle is hard?
Sami said, "I felt hopeless, but Dad helped me try again."
I never stay hopeless because I ask for help.

words.group: Words: the body, food and staying well
words.childMeaning: Living things, and the quality of being alive.
practiceSentences: There is life in every drop of pond water.
Is there life on any other planet?
Water is necessary for all life on Earth.
Life on the reef depends on clean water.
The scientist studies life in the deep ocean.

words.group: Words that say how often or how much
words.childMeaning: In most cases; usually.
practiceSentences: Fresh food is generally better than tinned.
Do you generally eat breakfast before school?
Children generally need more sleep than adults.
The market is generally busiest on Saturday.
Amal generally drinks water rather than juice.

words.group: Words that say how often or how much
words.childMeaning: For the most part; more than anything else.
practiceSentences: The soup is mainly vegetables and beans.
What is this bread mainly made from?
We mainly eat rice with our evening meal.
The illness is mainly spread by dirty hands.
Leo mainly drinks milk at breakfast.

words.group: Words that say how often or how much
words.childMeaning: True or happening most of the time, but not always.
practiceSentences: Omar works alone, but mostly a neighbour helps him.
Is the market mostly quiet in the morning?
Mostly, Amal enjoys writing her reports!
The shop stays mostly busy on market days.
The class mostly chose fruit for their snack.

words.childMeaning: A period of being unwell or having a disease.
practiceSentences: The nurse asked Noah how long the illness had lasted.
Can bad food cause a serious illness?
Grandma Hana nursed the whole family through the illness.
An illness like this can be avoided with clean food.
A few children laughed at first, until she reached the part about her illness.

words.childMeaning: Safety means being free from danger or harm.
practiceSentences: Let's practise our safety facts once more.
Do you know the safety rules for storms?
Amal's poster explained safety during lightning.
Time for a safety quiz!
Wear a helmet for safety when you ride your bike.

words.childMeaning: Feeling worried or a little afraid about something that might happen.
practiceSentences: My knees felt nervous as I waited behind the curtain.
Sami's hands shook because he was nervous about the recital.
Do new places make you feel nervous sometimes?
"Everyone gets nervous before a race," said the coach kindly.
I felt nervous when the dentist called my name.

words.childMeaning: Confident means you feel sure that you can do something.
practiceSentences: Amal felt confident before her speech.
Leo is confident when he reads aloud.
Practise makes you more confident.
She gave a confident smile to the class.
Nora was confident that her team would finish.

words.childMeaning: A period of one hundred years.
practiceSentences: Amal drew a timeline showing one whole century.
A century is one hundred years long.
What was school like a century ago?
Grandpa said, "Our old fort is over a century old."
I wonder what homes will look like next century.

words.childMeaning: A line that shows events in the order they happened.
practiceSentences: We drew a timeline of our school year.
Where does this event go on the timeline?
The timeline began with Amal's first day.
A timeline makes the order easy to see.

words.group: Words: measuring, maps and the world
words.childMeaning: Hard and firm, and not a liquid or a gas.
practiceSentences: Ice is water in a solid form.
Is this wall solid all the way through?
Amal built a solid tower of blocks.
A solid keeps its own shape.
The bridge rests on solid rock.

words.group: Words: measuring, maps and the world
words.childMeaning: Going the same way without bending or curving, like a ruler edge.
practiceSentences: Amal drew a straight line from one corner to the other.
Use a ruler to keep your lines straight.
Is the road to the market straight or curved?
The teacher said, "Stand in a straight line, please."
I folded the paper along a straight edge.

words.group: Prefixes: un-, re-, pre-, in- and dis-
words.childMeaning: Different from what people expect, or not common at all.
practiceSentences: It is unusual to see snow here.
What is unusual about this map?
An unusual bird appeared in the garden.
The unusual shape of the lake surprised us.
Nothing unusual happened during the journey.

words.group: Prefixes: un-, re-, pre-, in- and dis-
words.childMeaning: To write something again, in a better way.
practiceSentences: Rewrite the paragraph with shorter sentences.
Did you rewrite the opening line?
A rewrite often makes the meaning clearer.
She had to rewrite the label three times.
Rewrite means to write it again.

words.group: Prefixes: un-, re-, pre-, in- and dis-
words.childMeaning: A look at something before it is finished or shown.
practiceSentences: We had a preview of the school play.
Would you like a preview of the map?
The preview showed only the first page.
A preview helps you decide what to read.
Preview means to view it beforehand.

words.group: Prefixes: un-, re-, pre-, in- and dis-
words.childMeaning: Not correct, and not true.
practiceSentences: The second answer was incorrect.
Which measurement is incorrect?
An incorrect map can send you the wrong way.
He corrected the incorrect spelling.
An incorrect answer is not a disaster.

words.group: Prefixes: un-, re-, pre-, in- and dis-
words.childMeaning: To go out of sight so that nobody can see it.
practiceSentences: The path seemed to disappear into the mist.
Where did the boat disappear to?
The sun will disappear behind the hill soon.
Footprints disappear quickly in soft sand.
Stars disappear as the sky grows light.

words.childMeaning: Taking something into account before you judge.
practiceSentences: Considering the rain, the trip went well.
She runs very fast, considering her age.
The map is clear, considering how old it is.
Which route is best, considering the traffic?
We arrived early, considering the distance.

words.childMeaning: Not counting; leaving something out.
practiceSentences: The class has thirty pupils, excluding Leo.
What is the cost, excluding travel?
Excluding weekends, the trip takes four days.
The map shows every road, excluding footpaths.
Twelve came, excluding the two who were ill.

words.childMeaning: Coming right after this one; the next one.
practiceSentences: We will meet on the following Monday.
What happens in the following chapter?
Read the following instructions carefully.
The following day was much warmer.
Answer the following three questions.

words.childMeaning: Feeling unable to understand something clearly.
practiceSentences: Nora felt confused by the long instructions.
Are you confused about which street to take?
Poor Sami looked so confused after the test!
A clear headline stops readers from feeling confused.
The confused tourist asked Maya for directions.

words.childMeaning: Disappointed means sad because something did not happen as you hoped.
practiceSentences: Leo was disappointed when the trip was cancelled.
Amal felt disappointed with her score.
We were disappointed by the rain.
Do not be disappointed, you can try again.
Nora looked disappointed but smiled anyway.

words.childMeaning: Embarrassed means you feel shy because of something that happened.
practiceSentences: Leo was embarrassed when he tripped.
Amal felt embarrassed saying the wrong name.
Do not be embarrassed to ask for help.
Nora was embarrassed by the loud clapping.
He looked embarrassed and went very quiet.

words.childMeaning: Patient means able to wait calmly without getting upset.
practiceSentences: You learned to be patient.
Amal was patient while the paint dried.
A patient teacher explains it twice.
Be patient, the bus will come soon.
Leo is patient with his little brother.

words.childMeaning: To want to know something, and think about it.
practiceSentences: I wonder where Nora has gone.
Do you ever wonder how birds fly?
Amal began to wonder about the strange sound.
We wonder what the answer will be.
Sami looked at the stars in wonder.

words.childMeaning: Something that holds another thing up and stops it from falling.
practiceSentences: They added another support to the fence.
Is this support strong enough?
Add more stones for support, quickly!
We built a wooden support for the wall.
The shelf needs a stronger support.

words.childMeaning: A report is a piece of writing that describes facts about something.
practiceSentences: Sami helped Amal check her report for mistakes.
When is your report due, Maya?
What a well-written report this is!
Teacher Yasmin read the report aloud to the class.
Did that report help you?

words.childMeaning: A set of questions that shows what you have learned.
practiceSentences: We have a spelling test on Friday.
How did you find the maths test?
Amal revised hard for the test.
The test had twenty questions.
Sami passed the test with a high mark.

words.childMeaning: Doing well, or getting what you hoped for.
practiceSentences: The concert was very successful.
Was your experiment successful, Nora?
Amal was successful in the spelling contest.
A successful plan needs careful thought.
Sami felt successful after finishing the race.

words.childMeaning: Helpful, and good for doing a job.
practiceSentences: A ruler is a useful tool in maths.
Which book is most useful for spelling?
Amal gave some useful advice to Leo.
That was a useful lesson about plants.
A torch is useful when the power fails.

words.childMeaning: Made of wood, and not of metal or plastic.
practiceSentences: Nora leaned across the wooden desk.
Is this spoon wooden or metal?
Amal sat on the wooden bench outside.
A wooden gate leads into the garden.
Sami carved a small wooden bird.

words.childMeaning: More bad than something else.
practiceSentences: My handwriting is worse when I hurry.
Is the weather worse than yesterday?
Amal's cough grew worse during the night.
The second answer was worse than the first.
Nothing is worse than losing your book.

words.childMeaning: The most bad of all.
practiceSentences: That was the worst storm of the year.
Which is the worst day for a trip?
Amal's worst subject is spelling.
The worst part was waiting for the result.
Sami had the worst luck in the game.

words.childMeaning: The wild animals and plants of a place.
practiceSentences: The park protects wildlife of every kind.
What wildlife lives near your home?
Amal photographed the wildlife by the river.
Pollution harms the wildlife in the ocean.
Sami keeps a wildlife notebook.

words.childMeaning: The cause that explains why something happens or why you did it.
practiceSentences: Every idea in the box carries its own quiet reason.
There is a good reason for every class rule.
What is the reason the birds fly south?
Theo said, "The reason I smiled was your joke."
My reason for saving money is a new book.

words.childMeaning: A small fact or piece of information about something.
practiceSentences: Did you notice that small detail in the letter?
Omar explained each detail about his daily work.
What an interesting detail that is, Nora!
She checked every detail before sending her report.
She wanted it to be fair and honest, so she used every detail.

words.childMeaning: The subject or idea we talk or write about.
practiceSentences: Choosing a clear topic makes the writing much easier to plan.
Our writing topic today is helping our neighbours.
Which topic did you choose for your report?
Adam said, "My topic is life by the sea."
I picked rain as my topic for the poster.

words.group: im- and the people behind the work
words.childMeaning: Not able to be done or to happen.
practiceSentences: It is impossible to be in two places at once.
Why is that task impossible?
Nothing is impossible if you plan carefully.
An impossible deadline helps nobody.
Impossible means not possible.

words.group: im- and the people behind the work
words.childMeaning: A person who performs a role in a play or film.
practiceSentences: The actor learned every line by Friday.
Which actor played the narrator?
A good actor makes the audience believe.
Leo wants to be an actor one day.
The actor bowed at the end of the scene.

words.group: im- and the people behind the work
words.childMeaning: A woman or girl who performs a role in a play or film.
practiceSentences: The actress rehearsed her scene twice.
Who is the actress in the main role?
An actress must speak clearly on stage.
The actress remembered every single word.
Maya played the actress in our school drama.

words.group: im- and the people behind the work
words.childMeaning: A person who plays or writes music.
practiceSentences: The musician tuned her instrument.
Which musician wrote this song?
A musician practises for many hours.
The musician led the school orchestra.
Every musician in the band read the score.

words.group: im- and the people behind the work
words.childMeaning: The way somebody or something looks.
practiceSentences: The appearance of the stage changed completely.
How would you describe her appearance?
Do not judge a book by its appearance.
His sudden appearance surprised everyone.
The garden's appearance improves each spring.

words.group: im- and the people behind the work
words.childMeaning: An exciting experience or journey.
practiceSentences: The story tells of an adventure at sea.
What adventure would you choose?
Their adventure lasted three whole days.
Every adventure begins with a first step.
The book is an adventure from start to finish.

words.childMeaning: As a result of that.

Consequently, the plan had to change.

Consequently, our results were much clearer.

practiceSentences: The path was blocked; hence the long detour.

Hence, we decided to start earlier.

She had studied hard, hence her confidence.

words.childMeaning: In addition to what has been said.
practiceSentences: The plan is cheap; moreover, it is quick.
Moreover, the results were easy to check.

Moreover, every pupil agreed with the idea.
The book is short; moreover, it is well written.

words.childMeaning: As another choice instead.
practiceSentences: We could walk; alternatively, we could cycle.
Alternatively, could we take the bus?

Alternatively, the class could vote.
Use a metaphor; alternatively, try a simile.

words.childMeaning: A person who writes books or stories.

An author plans a story before writing it.
Did the author draw the pictures too?

I wrote to an author, and she wrote back!

words.childMeaning: A character is a person or animal in a story.
practiceSentences: The main character in the story is a fox.
Which character do you like best?
Amal drew every character from the book.
A character can change by the end of a story.
Leo wrote about a brave character.

words.childMeaning: The setting is the time and place where a story happens.
practiceSentences: The setting of the story is a small village.
What is the setting of this book?

The setting helps you picture the story.
A forest is the setting for this tale.

words.childMeaning: Something special that happens, like a party or a game.
practiceSentences: The neighbourhood event filled the park with music and laughter.

Which event are you entering on sports day?

I wore my best clothes to the school event.

words.childMeaning: A solution is the answer to a problem.
practiceSentences: Nora found a clever solution.
The solution was simpler than we thought.

Every problem has a solution somewhere.
Recycling is one solution to too much rubbish.

words.childMeaning: Facts or details about something.

The notice board shares information about the town fair.
What information do we need before planning the trip?
"Good information helps us make wise choices," said Father.
I found interesting information about bees in the encyclopedia.

words.childMeaning: Your opinion is what you think about something.
practiceSentences: In my opinion, the blue one is better.

Everybody has a different opinion.
What is your opinion of this poem?
An opinion is not the same as a fact.

words.childMeaning: A rhyme is a short poem with words that end in the same sound.

Which two words in this rhyme sound the same?

practiceSentences: Clap the rhythm of this poem.
The song has a fast rhythm.
Amal tapped the rhythm on the table.
Every poem has its own rhythm.
Leo found the rhythm hard to follow.

practiceSentences: Write one paragraph about your garden.
The first paragraph tells you where the story happens.
Amal started a new paragraph.
Each paragraph begins on a new line.
Leo read the last paragraph aloud.

practiceSentences: Can you retell the story to your partner?

It is easier to retell a story you enjoyed.

practiceSentences: Can you predict the ending of the story?

Look at the picture and predict what happens.
Leo could not predict who would win.
Scientists predict when the rain will come.

words.childMeaning: To talk about something with other people.
practiceSentences: Our class will discuss the plan for the reading wall.
Partners discuss their answers before telling the class.
Shall we discuss which game to play at break?
Theo said, "Let us discuss the ending of the story."
I discuss my drawings with my big sister.

words.childMeaning: A conversation is when two or more people talk together.
practiceSentences: Amal had a long conversation with her cousin.

Leo joined the conversation at lunch.
A good conversation needs careful listening.
Their conversation stopped when the bell rang.

words.childMeaning: To whisper means to speak very quietly.
practiceSentences: “Please forgive me,” said Nora in a whisper.
Amal had to whisper in the library.
Leo will whisper the answer to you.

Do not whisper while the teacher is talking.

words.childMeaning: All the letters we use, from A to Z.
practiceSentences: The alphabet has twenty-six letters.
Can you say the alphabet backwards?
Amal sang the alphabet with the class.
A dictionary follows the alphabet.
Sami wrote the whole alphabet neatly.

words.childMeaning: A small mark ( , ) used to show a pause or to separate items in a list.
practiceSentences: I wrote rice, lamb, and dates with a comma between them.
A comma tells the reader to pause for a moment.
Where should the comma go in this long sentence?

I forgot the comma, so my sentence looked confusing.

words.childMeaning: A sentence that tells somebody to do something.
practiceSentences: Sit down is a command.
Can you write a command sentence?
Amal used a command in her instructions.
A command often begins with a verb.
Close the door is a short command.

words.childMeaning: A book where you write what happens each day.
practiceSentences: Amal writes in her diary every night.
Where do you keep your diary?
The diary had a small silver lock.
Sami wrote about the trip in his diary.
A diary helps you remember details.

words.childMeaning: The rules for how we put words together to speak and write.
practiceSentences: The grammar contest tested verbs, questions, and small joining words.
Good grammar helps our sentences make sense.
Did you finish the grammar exercise on verbs?
The teacher said, "Check your grammar before handing in."
I am getting better at grammar every week.

words.childMeaning: A word that names a person, place or thing.
practiceSentences: School is a noun in that sentence.
Which noun names the animal?
Amal underlined every noun in red.
A noun can be a person, place or thing.
Sami wrote ten nouns in a list.

words.childMeaning: The form of a word that means more than one.
practiceSentences: Books is the plural of book.
What is the plural of child?
Amal wrote each plural correctly.
Most plurals end with the letter s.
The plural of foot is feet.

words.childMeaning: A person who reads, or a book used for reading.
practiceSentences: Amal is a fast and careful reader.
Which reader are we using this term?
A good reader stops to think.
Sami became a stronger reader this year.
Every reader chose a different book.

words.childMeaning: The correct order of letters in a word.
practiceSentences: Check the spelling before you finish.
Which spelling is right, Nora?
Amal won the spelling contest.
A dictionary shows you every spelling.
Sami practises his spelling each night.

words.childMeaning: A word that shows an action or a state.
practiceSentences: Run is a verb in that sentence.
Which verb tells you what she did?
Amal underlined every verb in blue.
A verb is often called an action word.
Sami listed ten verbs from the passage.

words.childMeaning: Things put out where people can see them.
practiceSentences: Our display shows work from every class.

Amal arranged the display by the door.
The museum display had ancient coins.
Sami stood beside his display table.
